props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both address managing cryptographic mechanisms: 800-171 requires establishing and managing cryptographic keys per defined requirements, directly overlapping with cm-3.6's mandate to keep crypto mechanisms under configuration management. | Both require implementing cryptographic mechanisms for CUI protection; 800-171 mandates specific crypto types while cm-3.6 requires those same mechanisms be under configuration management.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-08-09 requires cryptographic protection of CUI backup confidentiality, directly implementing cp-9's requirement to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of backup information. | 03-13-11 mandates FIPS-validated cryptography to protect CUI confidentiality, which overlaps with cp-9's requirement to protect backup information confidentiality using cryptographic mechanisms.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-13-08 implements cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI in storage, overlapping with cp-9.8's requirement to cryptographically protect backup information at primary and alternate storage locations. | 03-13-11 mandates implementing specific types of cryptography to protect CUI confidentiality, directly supporting the cryptographic mechanism requirement in cp-9.8 for backup information protection. | cp-9.8 notes organizations implementing crypto for backup must consider key management solutions, directly intersecting with 03-13-10's requirement to establish and manage cryptographic keys for generation, distribution, storage, and destruction.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Source establishes and manages cryptographic keys with access controls per applicable standards, intersecting with ia-7's requirement to authenticate operators to cryptographic modules with appropriate access controls. | Source implements cryptography in accordance with applicable laws, Executive Orders, and FIPS 140-3, directly meeting ia-7's requirement for cryptographic mechanisms meeting legal and standards requirements. | Source manages authenticators including for cryptographic devices and verifies identity of recipients, intersecting with ia-7's requirement to authenticate operators accessing cryptographic modules.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-01-02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access including remote access via external networks, intersecting with ac-17's authorization requirements. | 03-01-12 establishes usage restrictions, configuration requirements, and authorization for each type of remote access, directly implementing ac-17's core requirements. | 03-01-16 establishes usage restrictions and authorizes wireless access before connection, mirroring ac-17's requirements for wireless as a type of remote access. | 03-01-20 authorizes and restricts use of external systems and portable storage on external systems, overlapping with ac-17's authorization of remote connections through external networks. | 03-13-01 requires connecting to external systems only through managed boundary protection interfaces, directly supporting ac-17's control of remote access connection points. | 03-13-08 requires cryptographic mechanisms to protect CUI during transmission, implementing encrypted VPN/tunnel protections cited as a key mechanism in ac-17. | 03-13-11 mandates cryptographic protection for CUI confidentiality, supporting ac-17's reliance on encrypted VPNs and tunnels for secure remote connections.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both address cryptographic protection of CUI; 03-13-11 specifies types of cryptography that implement the confidentiality protection during transmission required by sc-8. | Both protect communications during transmission; sc-8 covers confidentiality and integrity broadly while 03-13-15 specifically protects authenticity of communications sessions, overlapping on integrity of transmitted data. | Both protect transmitted information: sc-8 broadly, and 03-10-08 via physical access controls on distribution and transmission lines to prevent eavesdropping and tampering. | Both require protecting CUI during transmission using cryptographic mechanisms, addressing confidentiality of transmitted information on internal and external networks.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both address cryptographic mechanisms protecting CUI; 03-13-10 establishes and manages the cryptographic keys that underpin the transmission encryption required by sc-8.1. | Both require implementing defined types of cryptography to protect CUI; 03-13-11 specifies the cryptographic types used, directly supporting the cryptographic protection during transmission required by sc-8.1.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both address cryptographic implementation for CUI; 03-13-11 specifies types of cryptography that depend on the key establishment and management processes defined in sc-12. | Both address cryptographic protection of CUI; 03-13-08 implements cryptographic mechanisms for transmission and storage that depend on the key establishment and management processes required by sc-12.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-13-11 and sc-13 both mandate implementing organization-defined types of cryptography in accordance with applicable laws and FIPS standards to protect CUI.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-13-11 requires implementing specific cryptography types to protect CUI confidentiality, near-identical to sc-28.1's mandate for cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of information at rest.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Authorized software deny-all/allow-by-exception policy identifies authorized software and blocks unauthorized execution, directly overlapping with preventing installation of unauthenticated software components. | Cryptographic key establishment and management establishes and manages cryptographic keys, directly supporting the cryptographic signing and verification mechanisms required to authenticate software and firmware before installation. | Cryptographic protection implements defined types of cryptography for protecting CUI, overlapping with the cryptographic mechanisms used to authenticate software and firmware components prior to installation. | Malicious code protection detects and eradicates malicious code at system entry and exit points, overlapping with preventing installation of unauthenticated or malicious software components. | Mobile code requirement authorizes, monitors, and controls the use of software programs and code, overlapping with controlling and authenticating code components prior to execution or installation.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03.01.12 establishes security requirements for remote system access connections, overlapping with ac-17.2's cryptographic protection of those connections. | 800-171 03.01.16 establishes connection and configuration requirements for wireless access including encryption, overlapping with ac-17.2's cryptographic protection of remote access sessions. | 800-171 03.01.18 requires full-device or container-based encryption for CUI on mobile devices used in remote connections, overlapping with ac-17.2's cryptographic protection of remote access. | 800-171 03.05.04 requires replay-resistant authentication for account access, overlapping with ac-17.2's integrity protection of remote access sessions. | 800-171 03.13.08 requires cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized CUI disclosure during transmission, directly overlapping with ac-17.2's encryption of remote access session confidentiality. | 800-171 03.13.11 requires implementing specified cryptographic types to protect CUI confidentiality, directly overlapping with ac-17.2's cryptographic mechanism requirement for remote sessions. | 800-171 03.13.15 protects authenticity of communications sessions, directly overlapping with ac-17.2's integrity protection of remote access sessions.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-18 establishes configuration and connection requirements for mobile devices, intersecting with AC-19(5)'s encryption mandate for mobile device data protection. | 800-171 03-13-08 mandates cryptographic mechanisms to protect CUI while in storage, directly supporting the device/container encryption requirement of AC-19(5). | 800-171 03-13-11 requires implementing specified types of cryptography to protect CUI confidentiality, directly implementing the encryption mechanism required by AC-19(5).

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both controls require defining account types, creating/enabling/modifying/disabling/removing accounts, specifying authorized users, group/role membership, and access authorizations.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-01 requires creating, enabling, modifying, disabling, and removing accounts per policy, covering the same lifecycle actions that ac-2.1 requires be performed via automated mechanisms.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-01 requires disabling and removing accounts per policy and criteria, covering the same account lifecycle management that ac-2.2 requires be automated for temporary and emergency accounts.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-01 requires disabling and removing accounts in accordance with policy, procedures, prerequisites, and criteria, directly implementing the account-disabling conditions specified in ac-2.3. | 800-171 03-09-02 requires disabling system access and revoking credentials upon termination or transfer, directly implementing ac-2.3's condition to disable accounts no longer associated with a user or individual.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03.01.01 requires creating, enabling, modifying, disabling, and removing accounts — exactly the actions that AC-2(4) mandates be automatically audited. | 800-171 03.03.01 specifies event types selected for logging, which must include account management events required by AC-2(4). | 800-171 03.03.02 specifies audit record content (event type, time, identity) that AC-2(4) account management audit records must capture. | 800-171 03.03.03 requires generating audit records for selected event types, directly covering account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions mandated by AC-2(4).

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03.01.01 creates accounts with specified prerequisites and criteria, implementing the usage conditions for accounts that AC-2(11) requires be defined and enforced. | 800-171 03.01.02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access per access control policies, directly implementing the usage condition enforcement that AC-2(11) requires. | 800-171 03.01.05 restricts access to only what is necessary for assigned tasks, operationally enforcing the least-privilege usage conditions AC-2(11) requires for system accounts.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03.01.01 explicitly requires disabling system accounts in accordance with criteria, directly implementing AC-2(13)'s requirement to disable accounts of high-risk individuals. | 800-171 03.09.02 requires disabling system access and revoking authenticators within a defined time period upon termination, paralleling AC-2(13)'s time-bounded account disabling for high-risk individuals.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Account management creates and manages user accounts with unique identifiers, providing the foundation for ia-2's user identification and authentication. | Authenticator management verifies identity during distribution and manages authenticator lifecycle, directly supporting ia-2's organizational user authentication requirement. | Identifier management assigns and manages unique identifiers for individuals and roles, directly implementing ia-2's requirement to uniquely identify organizational users. | Multi-factor authentication for privileged and non-privileged accounts directly implements the organizational user authentication requirement in ia-2. | Restricting privileged accounts to defined personnel requires identifying privileged users, directly intersecting with ia-2's unique identification and authentication of organizational users.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Source authorizes and verifies security requirements for external system users before granting access, directly intersecting with ia-8's requirement to authenticate non-organizational users accessing organizational systems. | Source creates and manages system accounts specifying authorized users and access authorizations, intersecting with ia-8's requirement to manage and authenticate non-organizational user accounts. | Source establishes authorization processes and verifies access authorizations for maintenance personnel who are typically non-organizational users, directly intersecting with ia-8's identification and authentication of non-organizational users. | Source manages unique identifiers for individuals, groups, roles, and devices including preventing reuse, directly supporting ia-8's requirement to uniquely identify non-organizational users. | Source requires MFA for all accounts including non-privileged, intersecting with ia-8's requirement to authenticate non-organizational users before granting system access. | Source requires uniquely identifying and authenticating all system users and associating unique IDs with processes, directly implementing ia-8's requirement for unique identification and authentication of non-organizational users. | Source verifies identity before issuing authenticators and manages authenticator distribution and revocation, intersecting with ia-8's management of authenticators for non-organizational users.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Account management creates accounts based on verified prerequisites; identity proofing provides the identity evidence validation required before account creation. | Authenticator management explicitly requires verifying identity before initial authenticator distribution, which is the core identity proofing activity described in ia-12. | Identifier management requires verifying identity and receiving authorization before assigning identifiers, directly overlapping with ia-12's requirement to resolve users to unique individuals. | Personnel screening requires verifying individual identity before authorizing system access, directly implementing the identity evidence collection and validation required by ia-12. | Uniquely identifying and authenticating users requires prior identity proofing to resolve each user to a unique individual, as both controls require.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-01 manages system account creation, modification, and removal — security functions explicitly listed in AC-6.1's discussion as requiring authorized access. | 800-171 03-01-02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access to CUI, overlapping with AC-6.1's mechanism of controlling who can exercise security-relevant permissions. | 800-171 03-01-04 defines system access authorizations to support separation of duties, intersecting with AC-6.1's requirement to authorize access to security functions to prevent conflict of interest. | 800-171 03-01-05 explicitly authorizes access to security functions, directly matching AC-6.1's requirement to authorize access to security functions and security-relevant information. | 800-171 03-01-06 restricts privileged accounts to defined personnel, directly implementing AC-6.1's requirement to authorize specific individuals' access to security functions. | 800-171 03-01-07 prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions and logs such execution, directly addressing AC-6.1's focus on controlling access to security functions like account management and auditing.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-01 manages account types including prohibition of certain accounts, directly supporting AC-6.2's requirement to define and enforce non-privileged account use for nonsecurity functions. | 800-171 03-01-02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access, overlapping with AC-6.2's control over which account type may access which system functions. | 800-171 03-01-04 defines access authorizations to support separation of duties, intersecting with AC-6.2's use of separate privileged and non-privileged accounts to enforce functional separation. | 800-171 03-01-05 allows only access necessary for assigned tasks, directly supporting AC-6.2's principle that privileged users must use non-privileged accounts for nonsecurity functions. | 800-171 03-01-07 prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions, complementing AC-6.2's requirement that privileged users use non-privileged accounts for nonsecurity work.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-01 defines types of accounts allowed/prohibited and manages account lifecycle, directly supporting AC-6.5's restriction of privileged accounts to defined roles. | 800-171 03-01-02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access, overlapping with AC-6.5's enforcement of privileged account restrictions. | 800-171 03-01-04 defines access authorizations to support separation of duties, intersecting with AC-6.5's restriction of privileged accounts to prevent inappropriate concentration of privilege. | 800-171 03-01-05 allows only access necessary for assigned tasks, providing the least-privilege principle underlying AC-6.5's restriction of privileged accounts. | 800-171 03-01-07 prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions and logs such execution, directly supporting AC-6.5's restriction of privileged accounts to appropriate personnel.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-01 reviews, modifies, and removes accounts based on organizational needs, directly implementing AC-6.7's requirement to reassign or remove privileges when no longer justified. | 800-171 03-01-04 defines access authorizations to support separation of duties, intersecting with AC-6.7's review and reassignment of privileges to reflect current organizational needs. | 800-171 03-01-05 requires access only necessary for assigned tasks, directly supporting AC-6.7's periodic review to validate whether assigned privileges remain necessary. | 800-171 03-01-06 restricts privileged accounts to defined personnel, directly supporting AC-6.7's validation that privileged assignments remain appropriate and correctly scoped. | 800-171 03-01-07 controls execution of privileged functions, intersecting with AC-6.7's review and potential removal of privileges that are no longer mission-justified. | 800-171 03-09-02 terminates/revokes authenticators and system access upon employment termination or transfer, directly implementing AC-6.7's reassignment or removal of privileges when organizational roles change. | 800-171 03-12-01 assesses security requirements at defined frequency to determine if satisfied, overlapping with AC-6.7's periodic review of assigned privileges to validate continued necessity.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-05-01 manages user identifiers and authenticators; revoking authenticators and credentials upon termination directly implements PS-4's revocation requirement. | Account Management's requirement to disable and remove system accounts directly implements PS-4's mandate to disable system access upon individual termination.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03.01.01 requires modifying and disabling system accounts in accordance with organizational procedures, implementing ps-5's requirement to adjust logical access authorizations upon personnel transfer. | 800-171 03.09.02 explicitly covers personnel transfer — reviewing access authorizations, retrieving property, and modifying access — directly implementing ps-5's transfer requirements. | 800-171 03.10.01 requires maintaining and reviewing physical access authorization lists, overlapping with ps-5's requirement to confirm ongoing need for physical access during transfers.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-01-02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access to CUI, which includes verifying write permissions before accepting data transfers as required by ca-3.6. | 03-01-03 enforces approved authorizations for controlling CUI flow within and between connected systems, directly implementing ca-3.6's requirement to verify transfer authorizations before accepting data. | 03-01-05 restricts system access to only what is necessary for assigned tasks, directly supporting ca-3.6's requirement that transferring parties hold the specific write permissions needed. | 03-01-20 requires authorization before use of external systems, intersecting with ca-3.6's verification that transferring systems have requisite privileges before data acceptance. | 03-13-04 prevents unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources, directly overlapping with ca-3.6's goal of preventing unauthorized inter-system data transfers.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both control privileged functions on the system; 800-171 prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions, intersecting with cm-5's enforcement that only authorized users can make configuration changes. | Both enforce approved authorizations for logical access; 800-171 access enforcement for CUI and system resources directly overlaps with cm-5's requirement to enforce logical access restrictions for system changes. | Both enforce physical access controls to protect system components; 800-171 physical access control verifies authorizations at facility entry/exit, directly overlapping with cm-5's physical access restrictions for system changes. | Both require approving configuration changes and restricting who can make them; 800-171 configuration change control requires review and approval of changes, directly intersecting with cm-5's define, approve, and enforce change access restrictions. | Both restrict privileged access to defined personnel; 800-171 restricts privileged accounts to defined roles, directly intersecting with cm-5's requirement to restrict change access to authorized individuals. | Both restrict system access to only authorized users performing assigned tasks; 800-171 least privilege limits access to necessary capabilities, intersecting with cm-5's access restrictions that limit who may make system changes.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 enforces approved authorizations for logical access to CUI, directly implementing the access enforcement mechanism required by cm-5.1. | 800-171 requires defining and enforcing physical and logical access restrictions for changes, directly implementing cm-5.1's mandate to enforce access restrictions. | 800-171 requires generating and retaining audit records for selected event types, directly satisfying cm-5.1's requirement to automatically generate audit records of enforcement actions. | 800-171 requires logging the execution of privileged functions, overlapping with cm-5.1's mandate to auto-generate audit records of access enforcement actions. | 800-171 restricts system access to only what is necessary for assigned tasks, implementing the access restriction enforcement that cm-5.1 requires to be automated. | 800-171's deny-all, allow-by-exception policy for authorized software enforces access restrictions on software execution, intersecting with cm-5.1's automated access enforcement requirement.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both controls enforce approved authorizations for logical access to system resources in accordance with access control policies, differing only in 800-171's CUI scope.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access to CUI, overlapping with AC-6.3's requirement to authorize only specific network access to privileged commands. | 800-171 03-01-05 restricts access to only what is necessary for assigned tasks, overlapping with AC-6.3's authorization of network access to privileged commands only for compelling operational needs. | 800-171 03-01-06 restricts privileged accounts to defined personnel, intersecting with AC-6.3's requirement to limit network access to privileged commands to specific authorized individuals. | 800-171 03-01-07 prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions, overlapping with AC-6.3's restriction of network access to privileged commands to authorized users only. | 800-171 03-01-12 establishes usage restrictions and authorizes each type of remote access, directly intersecting with AC-6.3's control of network access to privileged commands. | 800-171 03-13-01 monitors and controls communications at external and internal interfaces, overlapping with AC-6.3's requirement to control network access channels through which privileged commands flow. | 800-171 03-13-06 denies network communications by default and allows by exception, directly implementing AC-6.3's approach of limiting network access to privileged commands to specific documented cases.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access, providing the access control mechanism that prevents non-privileged users from reaching privileged functions as required by AC-6(10). | 800-171 03-01-05 least privilege requires authorizing access to security functions only to designated roles, overlapping with AC-6(10)'s restriction of privileged function execution to authorized users. | 800-171 03-01-06 restricts privileged accounts to defined personnel and requires use of non-privileged accounts for non-security functions, directly supporting AC-6(10)'s prohibition on non-privileged users executing privileged functions.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03.01.02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access in accordance with access control policies, which are established through the access agreements required by ps-6. | 800-171 03.01.20 requires establishing security requirements satisfied on external systems prior to access, paralleling ps-6's requirement to verify signed access agreements before granting system access. | 800-171 03.12.05 requires interconnection security agreements and information exchange agreements before exchanging CUI, directly implementing ps-6's requirement to sign access agreements before granting system access.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-01-02 requires enforcing approved access control authorizations, which implements the authorization mechanism ra-5.5 requires before granting privileged access for vulnerability scanning. | 03-01-05 requires authorizing access only as necessary for assigned tasks, directly implementing the principle of authorized privileged access that ra-5.5 requires for vulnerability scanning activities. | 03-01-06 requires restricting privileged accounts to defined personnel and mandating their use only when needed, directly implementing the privileged access authorization controls ra-5.5 requires for scanning. | 03-01-07 requires preventing non-privileged users from executing privileged functions and logging their execution, directly implementing the privileged access authorization mechanism ra-5.5 mandates for intrusive scanning. | 03-11-02 requires vulnerability scanning including privileged access mechanisms, directly implementing the scanning activity for which ra-5.5 requires privileged access authorization.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 enforces approved access authorizations for logical access to CUI and system resources, supporting SC-2's requirement to enforce boundaries between user and system management functionality. | 800-171 limits system access to what is necessary for assigned tasks, intersecting with SC-2's requirement to separate user-facing functionality from privileged system management operations. | 800-171 prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions and logs privileged function execution, directly implementing SC-2's separation of system management functionality from general user functionality. | 800-171 requires configuring systems to provide only mission-essential capabilities and restricting unnecessary functions and services, directly supporting SC-2's separation of user and system management functionality. | 800-171 requires identifying duties requiring separation and defining access authorizations to support separation of duties, overlapping with SC-2's requirement to separate system management functionality from user functionality. | 800-171 restricts privileged accounts to defined personnel and requires use of non-privileged accounts for non-administrative activities, directly supporting SC-2's separation of system management from user-level access.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03.01.02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access, overlapping with ac-17.3's requirement to route remote access through authorized control points. | 800-171 03.01.03 enforces authorizations controlling CUI flow between connected systems, overlapping with ac-17.3's routing of remote access through managed control points. | 800-171 03.01.12 explicitly requires routing remote access through authorized and managed connections, directly matching ac-17.3's managed network access control points requirement. | 800-171 03.01.20 prohibits use of external systems unless specifically authorized, overlapping with ac-17.3's requirement to authorize and manage remote access entry points. | 800-171 03.13.01 monitors and controls communications at external managed interfaces, directly overlapping with ac-17.3's managed network access control points for remote access. | 800-171 03.13.06 denies network communications by default and allows by exception, supporting ac-17.3's requirement for managed network access control points for remote access.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03.01.02 enforces approved authorizations for CUI and system resources, overlapping with ac-17.4's requirement to authorize security-relevant information access via remote access. | 800-171 03.01.05 authorizes access only to security functions necessary for tasks, overlapping with ac-17.4's authorization of privileged command execution via remote access. | 800-171 03.01.06 restricts privileged accounts to defined personnel and requires non-privileged accounts for non-security functions, directly overlapping with ac-17.4's privileged command authorization. | 800-171 03.01.07 prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions and logs execution, directly overlapping with ac-17.4's authorization and auditing of privileged commands via remote access. | 800-171 03.01.12 authorizes remote access and routes it through managed connections, directly overlapping with ac-17.4's requirement to authorize privileged commands via remote access. | 800-171 03.03.08 protects audit information and limits audit management to privileged users, overlapping with ac-17.4's assessable evidence requirement for privileged remote commands.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 03-01-02 enforces approved authorizations for logical access to CUI resources, supporting AC-21's requirement to verify sharing partner access authorizations match information use restrictions. | 800-171 03-01-03 enforces approved authorizations for controlling CUI flow between connected systems, directly supporting AC-21's mechanism of verifying access authorizations match sharing partner restrictions. | 800-171 03-12-05 approves and manages CUI exchange between systems using interconnection and information exchange security agreements, directly implementing AC-21's information sharing authorization framework. | 800-171 03-13-04 prevents unauthorized information transfer via shared system resources, intersecting with AC-21's requirement to verify that sharing partner authorizations match information use restrictions before sharing.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-01-03 enforces approved authorizations for controlling CUI flow between connected systems, directly supporting the access-control dimension of ca-3's information exchange management. | 03-01-20 prohibits unauthorized external system use and establishes security requirements before connectivity, directly intersecting with ca-3's approval and management of inter-system exchanges. | 03-16-03 requires external system service providers to comply with defined security requirements, overlapping with ca-3's mandate to document security requirements for each system exchange.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both controls enforce approved authorizations for controlling information/CUI flow within and between connected systems using identical information flow control mechanisms.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Information flow enforcement controls where CUI flows within and between systems, directly overlapping with SC-4's requirement to prevent unauthorized info transfer via shared resources.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-01-03 enforces approved authorizations controlling flow of CUI between connected systems, overlapping with sc-7.4's traffic flow policy at managed interfaces. | 03-01-12 requires routing remote access through authorized managed connections and establishing connection requirements, overlapping with sc-7.4's managed interface and traffic flow controls. | 03-12-05 requires approving and managing exchange of CUI between systems via agreements, overlapping with sc-7.4's requirement to manage and document information exchange across external telecommunications interfaces. | 03-13-06 denies network traffic by default and allows by exception, directly implementing the traffic flow policy required by sc-7.4 at managed interfaces. | 03-13-08 uses cryptographic mechanisms to protect confidentiality and integrity of CUI during transmission, directly addressing sc-7.4's requirement to protect information across managed interfaces. | 03-14-06 monitors inbound and outbound communications traffic for unauthorized activity, overlapping with sc-7.4's requirement to control and review communications at managed interfaces. | 03-16-03 requires external system service providers to comply with security requirements, intersecting with sc-7.4's governance of external telecommunications service interfaces. | Both require monitoring and controlling communications at external managed interfaces, directly addressing sc-7.4's managed interface and traffic flow requirements.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-01-03 enforces approved authorizations controlling the flow of CUI within and between systems, sharing the allow-by-exception operational mechanism with sc-7.5's deny-by-default network policy. | 03-01-12 requires authorizing each type of remote access before establishing connections, implementing an allow-by-exception approach that intersects with sc-7.5's deny-by-default network traffic policy. | 03-13-01 monitors and controls communications at managed interfaces, which is the enforcement mechanism underlying the deny-by-default policy in sc-7.5.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-01-03 enforces authorized information flow controls between connected systems, overlapping with sc-7.7's requirement to prevent unauthorized dual-path communication via split tunneling. | 03-01-12 requires routing remote access through authorized and managed connections, directly addressing sc-7.7's requirement to prevent split tunneling by controlling remote device traffic paths. | 03-13-01 monitors and controls communications at external managed interfaces, intersecting with sc-7.7's requirement to control remote device tunneling through managed boundaries.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-01-03 enforces approved authorizations controlling CUI flow between connected systems, overlapping with sc-7.8's proxy-based enforcement of authorized traffic routing at managed interfaces. | 03-01-12 requires routing remote access through authorized and managed connections, paralleling sc-7.8's requirement to route internal and external traffic through authenticated proxy servers. | 03-13-01 requires monitoring and controlling communications at managed interfaces, directly intersecting with sc-7.8's requirement to route traffic through authenticated proxy servers at managed interfaces. | 03-13-06 denies network communications by default and allows by exception, complementing sc-7.8's authenticated proxy enforcement by ensuring only authorized traffic is routed through managed interfaces.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both enforce separation of information flows using boundary protection devices such as routers, gateways, firewalls, and encrypted tunnels between system components. | Both require boundary protection via gateways, routers, firewalls, virtualization, and subnetworks to isolate and control communications between system components.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both controls identify duties requiring separation and define system access authorizations to support separation of duties, using near-identical language and mechanisms.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 800-171 prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions, restricting available system functions by role in alignment with cm-7's least-functionality requirement. | 800-171 prohibits use of external systems unless specifically authorized, implementing cm-7's requirement to restrict use of unauthorized functions and external connections. | 800-171 requires establishing configuration settings in the most restrictive mode, implementing the same restrictive configuration posture required by cm-7 for functions and services. | 800-171 requires establishing usage restrictions and configuration requirements for remote access connections, implementing cm-7's mandate to restrict ports, protocols, and services. | 800-171 requires establishing usage restrictions and configuration requirements for wireless access, implementing cm-7's mandate to restrict connections and services. | 800-171 requires monitoring and controlling communications at external and internal interfaces, implementing cm-7's restriction of ports, protocols, and services at system boundaries. | 800-171 restricts system access to only what is necessary for assigned tasks, applying the same least-functionality principle that cm-7 mandates for system capabilities and services. | 800-171's deny-all, allow-by-exception policy for authorized software directly implements cm-7's requirement to prohibit or restrict unauthorized software and services.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: 03-01-05 limits access to only what is necessary for assigned tasks, directly implementing the authorized-access enforcement that AC-3 requires.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both controls restrict system access to only what is authorized and necessary for users' assigned organizational tasks, using near-identical language to express the least-privilege principle.

props.name: mapping-rationale
